newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares rose in hectic trade to close strong in record volumes. Industrials were firm riding on the back of firm Wall Street and golds leapt on a $6 recovery in the bullion price.
Dealers said sentiment was positive boosted by the steady rand and a bouyant bonds market. They said Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's comments were bullish for the market.

"Everything is going in the right direction. Bonds are unbelievable and we had good comments from the government. The market should still keep on going. Foreigners are very interested in the market," a dealer said.

Presenting his Appropriations Adjustment Bill in parliament, Manuel said the government had revised its 1996/97 expenditure upwards by 2.4 billion rand to 176.1 billion rand but was still on target to achieve a deficit of 5.1 percent of gross domestic product.
At 1500 GMT prices were still updating on the Reuter Terminals after a communications fault.
The JSE said the all-share index ended up 70 points to 6,966 points, industrials gained 70 points to 8,263 points and the gold index made 40 points to 1,350 points.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange said volumes traded on the exchange had soared to a record 1.45 billion rand. Dealers said they were boosted by a corporate finance deal in Norwich valued at 659 million rand.
Gold shares staged a recovery on Thursday after interest in New York ovenight pushed them up six to seven percent.

"Gold shares are a lot better...As long as the gold price holds these levels we could see a recovery. The gold price is volatile but there should be good interest in New York tonight. They won't push them up just support them," one said.
Dealers said the market should continue firm on Friday after consolidating on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"The market should continue bullish tomorrow. We had two or three days of consolidation and we are back on track now," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
De Beers last shed 200 cents to 148.75 rand, Anglo made 700 cents to 277 rand, Dries was up 95 cents to 44.25 rand and Vaal Reefs added 12 rand to 305 rand.

Near-dated gold share futures ended firmer, but off their highs after the yellow metal staged a recovery. Industrial contracts rose on a better on a strong Wall Street on Wednesday. The March all-share contract was up 6,475/850 from 6,431, the industrial contract was at 8,076/83 from 8,020 and the gold contract was at 975/79 from 957.
